title: Valdés Peninsula: whales and marine wildlife
meta_description: Valdés Peninsula guide: whale watching, sea lions, elephant seals, penguins, when to go, how to get there and where to stay.
hero_subtitle: One of the best places in the world to see whales from shore and at sea.
photo_alt: Southern right whale at Valdés Peninsula

why_visit.title: Southern right whale
why_visit.text: Every year they arrive in the gulfs to breed; the season runs roughly from June to December.

why_visit.title: Wildlife all year
why_visit.text: Sea lions and elephant seals live on the peninsula's shores much of the year.

why_visit.title: World Heritage Site
why_visit.text: The peninsula is recognized by UNESCO for the importance of its marine wildlife.

activities.title: Whale-watching boat trips
activities.text: In season, boat trips leave from Puerto Pirámides, the only town on the peninsula.

activities.title: Whales from shore
activities.text: In parts of the gulf, such as the coast near Puerto Madryn, whales come very close to shore.

activities.title: Driving around the peninsula
activities.text: Wildlife viewpoints such as Punta Delgada, Caleta Valdés and Punta Norte, linked by gravel roads.

activities.title: Penguins
activities.text: In spring and summer, Magellanic penguins arrive on the Chubut coast; Punta Tombo, to the south, is one of the best-known colonies.

activities.title: Puerto Madryn
activities.text: The base town, with a waterfront, beaches and diving in Golfo Nuevo.

how_to_get_there:
By plane: the most used airports are Trelew (REL) and Puerto Madryn (PMY). From Trelew it's about an hour by road to Puerto Madryn.

By bus: long-distance services reach Puerto Madryn from Buenos Aires and other cities.

On the peninsula: explore on a tour from Puerto Madryn or by car. Inner roads are gravel: drive carefully.

where_to_stay.budget: Hostels with shared rooms and guest kitchens, plus campsites in season. They're the most affordable option and a good place to meet other travelers.
where_to_stay.midrange: Inns, cabins and small hotels, often with breakfast included. Cabins with kitchens suit families and groups.
where_to_stay.luxury: Upscale hotels and lodges with landscape views, spas or tours included. Book them well in advance.

practical_tips.title: When to go
practical_tips.text: For whales, roughly June to December. Animal cycles vary a little each year: check before you travel.

practical_tips.title: Changeable weather
practical_tips.text: Wind and sudden weather changes are part of the trip. Dress in layers and always carry a windbreaker.

practical_tips.title: Book ahead
practical_tips.text: In high season, lodging and tours fill up. It's best to book as soon as you have your dates.

practical_tips.title: Prices and payments
practical_tips.text: Prices change often: check current rates before you travel and carry some cash as well as cards.

closing: Plan at least two days: one for a whale-watching trip and another to explore the peninsula at a relaxed pace.
